Here are the two ways to load settings side by side:

````columns
### Before
Settings are read once at startup in src/session/settings.ts.

- One read, no watcher
- Changes need a restart

```ts
const settings = readSettings()
export function get(key: string) {
  return settings[key]
}
```
---
### After
Settings live in a store that reloads when the file changes.

- Watches the file
- Changes apply at once

<details>
<summary>Cleanup on exit</summary>

The watcher is closed when the app quits, so no handle is left open.

</details>

```ts
const store = createStore(readSettings())
watch(path, () => {
  store.set(readSettings())
})
```
````

Each one fits a different kind of app:

```columns
### Small tools
- Read once
- No watcher needed
---
### Editors
- Reload on change
- Keep the old value on errors
- Show a notice
---
### Servers
- Reload on a signal
- Log every reload
```
